query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Improving dynamic strength-ductility performance in high-entropy alloys through grain refinement
generation.conditions: high strain rates and low temperatures
generation.mechanism: grain refinement leads to increased grain boundary area, which enhances dislocation pinning and improves strength-ductility balance
generation.boundary: high strain rates and low temperatures
generation.uncertainty: limited understanding of the underlying mechanisms
generation.falsification_experiment: compare the dynamic strength-ductility performance of grain-refined and untreated high-entropy alloys under high strain rates and low temperatures
